pull_requests.title: CASE expressions in SELECT without FROM
pull_requests.description:
Closes #24

Ticket: https://github.com/bettersandeep/lekha/issues/24

Acceptance criteria from the ticket:
- [ ] `CASE WHEN <cond> THEN <result> [WHEN ...] [ELSE <result>] END` gives the result of the first WHEN whose condition is true. A condition is true when it is not 0 and not NULL. With no true condition it gives the ELSE result, or NULL when there is no ELSE.
- [ ] `CASE <base> WHEN <value> THEN <result> [WHEN ...] [ELSE <result>] END` gives the result of the first WHEN whose value equals the base. A NULL base or a NULL value never matches.
- [ ] A CASE can be inside each expression that the engine supports and can hold each of them, another CASE and an aggregate included.
- [ ] The keywords are case-insensitive. A CASE with no WHEN, a WHEN with no THEN and a missing END are errors.
- [ ] An error inside one part of a CASE is an error for the whole statement, also in a part that SQLite does not evaluate. This is the same decision as for COALESCE in ticket #10.
- [ ] `iif` and each other function that is not there today stay errors.
- [ ] `tests/slt/baseline.txt` has the new exact pass count. The number goes up.
- [ ] No record that passed before fails now.

Score: 8995 -> 9644 of 10012

Opened by the yantra runner. A person merges.

<details>
<summary>Report of agent start 1, as plain text</summary>

```text
# Report: ticket #24, CASE expressions in SELECT without FROM

## 1. What changed

- `src/select.rs`
  - New `Parser::case`, called from `unary` before the function-call arm, so `CASE (1) WHEN ...` is not read as a call.
  - It computes every part (base, each WHEN, each THEN, the ELSE), so an error in any part fails the statement.
  - New helper `Parser::at` (peek for a keyword without consuming it); `keyword` now uses it.
  - Module comment and the `unary` doc comment name CASE, with the SQLite source (lang_expr.html section 7, plus SQLite 3.46.1 answers).
  - Six new `case_` tests. Removed `SELECT CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 END` from `unsupported_input_is_an_error`.
- `tests/slt/baseline.txt`: 8995 → 9644.
- `README.md`: Status section describes CASE; score line is 9644 of 10012.

The last `yt check` passed: fmt, clippy, 43 unit tests, 10 harness tests, `slt: random/expr/slt_good_0.test 9644/10012`.

Expected values in the tests come from `yt sqlite .yt/q.sql` (SQLite 3.46.1, 54 statements), and three are records of the test file (lines 93, 199, 1576).

## 2. Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Check that I ran | Result that I saw |
|---|---|---|
| CASE without a base: first true WHEN, else ELSE, else NULL; true is not 0 and not NULL | Test `case_without_a_base_takes_the_first_true_when`; same statements in `yt sqlite` | Pass. For example `CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 END, CASE WHEN 0 THEN 2 END, CASE WHEN NULL THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, CASE WHEN - 1 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END` gives `2, NULL, 3, 2` in both |
| CASE with a base: first WHEN equal to the base; NULL base or NULL value never matches | Test `case_with_a_base_takes_the_first_equal_when`; same statements in `yt sqlite` | Pass. For example `CASE NULL WHEN NULL THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, CASE 1 WHEN NULL THEN 1 WHEN 1 THEN 5 END` gives `2, 5` in both |
| CASE inside each supported expression and holding each of them, another CASE and an aggregate included | Test `case_with_each_other_expression`: arithmetic, comparison, `NOT`, `AND`/`OR`, `IS NULL`, parentheses, `COALESCE`, `NULLIF`, `CAST`, nested CASE, aggregates on both sides | Pass. `MAX(CASE WHEN 1 THEN COUNT(*) END)` is "misuse of aggregate function COUNT"; SQLite also gives an error |
| Keywords case-insensitive; no WHEN, WHEN with no THEN, missing END are errors | Tests `case_keywords_ignore_case_and_white_space` and `case_errors` (29 statements) | Pass. `CASE 1 END` gives `unsupported syntax at Word("END")`; `CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2` gives `unexpected end of the statement` |
| An error in one part is an error for the statement, also in a part SQLite does not evaluate | Test `error_in_a_part_of_a_case_is_an_error` (15 statements) | Pass. `CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 ELSE abs(-9223372036854775807 - 1) END` is an error here; SQLite gives 2 |
| `iif` and each other absent function stay errors | Same test, 4 `iif` statements; existing `each_other_function_is_an_error` | Pass |
| Baseline has the new exact count, and it goes up | `yt check` | 8995 → 9644, and the test passes with the new baseline |
| No record that passed before fails now | No per-record comparison run; I did not have a tool for it | Not measured directly. Argument: before this change every statement with the word `CASE` was an error; the file has 0 `statement error` records (grep), so no such record could pass. For statements without `CASE` the only code change is the `at` refactor of `keyword`, and all earlier unit tests still pass |

## 3. Known differences from SQLite

All are errors here where SQLite 3.46.1 gives a value; none returns a different value.

- Unevaluated parts: SQLite stops at the first match. `CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 ELSE 9223372036854775807 + 1 END` and `CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 WHEN abs(...) THEN 3 END` give 2 there. This is the decision the ticket asks for.
- `SELECT CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 END END` and `SELECT 1 AS end`: SQLite accepts `END` as an alias. The engine rejects every keyword as an alias (existing rule).
- `CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 END NOT NULL`: SQLite gives 1. Postfix `NOT NULL` was already unsupported.
- Nesting: each CASE is one level of the existing 100-level limit; SQLite permits 1000.

## 4. Text for new tickets

- 368 records still fail in `random/expr/slt_good_0.test`. I saw these causes and did not count them:
  - `CREATE TABLE` and `INSERT` (lines 3 to 36).
  - `CAST(... AS REAL)` inside a CASE (line 368).
  - `AVG` (lines 712, 724, 872).
- Lazy evaluation of CASE and COALESCE, so a part that SQLite does not compute cannot fail the statement. It needs a parser that builds a tree before it evaluates.
- `END` (and the other keywords that SQLite accepts as fallback identifiers) as an alias.
- A per-record regression check in the runner or in `yt`: compare the set of passing records before and after, so "no record that passed before fails now" is measured instead of argued.

## 5. Review findings

Not a review round.
```

</details>

generated_descriptions.short_why: Support for CASE expressions was missing in SELECT statements without a FROM clause, causing valid SQLite-style queries to fail. This PR addresses ticket #24 by adding SQLite-compatible CASE handling while preserving existing unsupported-function behavior.
generated_descriptions.short_how: Implemented CASE parsing and evaluation in src/select.rs, including searched and simple forms, truthiness/matching rules, nesting, and syntax/error handling. Added parser helpers, expanded tests for CASE behavior and edge cases, updated README documentation, and refreshed the SLT baseline in tests/slt/baseline.txt.
generated_descriptions.long:
## Summary

This PR adds support for `CASE` expressions in `SELECT` statements without a `FROM` clause, closing ticket #24.

Before this change, `CASE ... END` was treated as unsupported syntax and always failed. The ticket required implementing SQLite-like `CASE` behavior, including both searched and simple forms, correct truthiness and matching rules, case-insensitive keywords, nesting, and strict error handling. It also required preserving existing behavior for unsupported functions such as `iif`, and updating the SLT baseline score.

## Why this was needed

The engine already supported a range of scalar expressions, but `CASE` was missing entirely. That caused any query using `CASE` to fail, including valid expressions that should have returned values under SQLite-compatible semantics.

The ticket specifically required:

- searched `CASE WHEN ... THEN ...` semantics
- simple `CASE base WHEN value THEN ...` semantics
- support for nested `CASE` and `CASE` inside any supported expression
- case-insensitive keywords
- syntax errors for malformed `CASE` forms
- eager evaluation of all parts of `CASE`, even parts SQLite would not evaluate
- keeping unsupported functions like `iif` as errors

## How it was implemented

### Parser changes in `src/select.rs`

The main implementation is in the expression parser:

- Added a new `Parser::case` method to parse and evaluate `CASE` expressions.
- Hooked `CASE` into `unary()` so it is recognized as an expression form before function-call parsing.
- Added a small helper `Parser::at()` to check the next keyword without consuming it, and updated `keyword()` to use it.

### `CASE` evaluation behavior

The new parser logic handles both forms:

- `CASE WHEN <cond> THEN <result> ... [ELSE <result>] END`
  - chooses the first true condition
  - treats a condition as true only when it is not `0` and not `NULL`

- `CASE <base> WHEN <value> THEN <result> ... [ELSE <result>] END`
  - compares each `WHEN` value to the base
  - `NULL` never matches, either as the base or as a `WHEN` value

It also follows the ticket’s requirement that each part of the `CASE` is computed independently, so errors inside any branch still fail the entire statement even if SQLite would normally short-circuit that branch.

### Tests added

A large set of tests was added in `src/select.rs`, covering:

- searched `CASE` behavior
- simple `CASE` behavior
- nested `CASE`
- `CASE` inside and around other supported expressions
- aggregates inside `CASE` and `CASE` inside aggregates
- case-insensitive keywords and whitespace handling
- syntax errors for malformed `CASE`
- error propagation from unevaluated branches
- unsupported `iif` function behavior
- nesting-depth limits

One previously invalid test case, `SELECT CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 END`, was removed from the “unsupported input is an error” test set because it is now supported.

### Documentation and baseline updates

- `README.md` was updated to document `CASE` support, its semantics, and the new score.
- `tests/slt/baseline.txt` was updated from `8995` to `9644` passing records.

## Affected areas

### Parser / expression evaluation
- `src/select.rs`
  - `Parser::case`
  - `Parser::at`
  - `Parser::keyword`
  - `Parser::unary`

### Tests
- `src/select.rs` test module
  - new `case_*` test coverage
  - updated unsupported-input expectations

### Documentation
- `README.md`
  - supported expression list
  - `CASE` semantics
  - score update

### Baseline / acceptance data
- `tests/slt/baseline.txt`
  - new pass count

## Result

This change makes `CASE` expressions valid and test-covered in `SELECT` statements without `FROM`, while preserving existing unsupported-function behavior and improving SQLite compatibility for expression handling.

pull_requests.title: Comparison and boolean operators in SELECT without FROM
pull_requests.description:
Closes #20

Ticket: https://github.com/bettersandeep/lekha/issues/20

Acceptance criteria from the ticket:
- [ ] `=`, `==`, `<>`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` between two integer values give 1 or 0. A NULL operand gives NULL.
- [ ] `NOT`, `AND` and `OR` follow SQLite's three-valued logic. A value is true when it is not 0 and not NULL. `NULL AND 0` is 0, `NULL OR 1` is 1, and `NOT NULL` is NULL.
- [ ] `<expr> IS NULL` and `<expr> IS NOT NULL` give 1 or 0, never NULL.
- [ ] The precedence is the one in the table above, and operators of one row group from left to right.
- [ ] A result is an integer. It can be an operand of arithmetic, an argument of a function and the argument of an aggregate.
- [ ] Each other operator of that document is an error for now: `~`, `||`, the bit operators, `BETWEEN`, `IN`, `LIKE`, `GLOB`, `ISNULL`, `NOTNULL`, `NOT NULL` as a postfix, `IS DISTINCT FROM`, and `IS` or `IS NOT` with a right side that is not `NULL`.
- [ ] `tests/slt/baseline.txt` has the exact pass count. The number does not go down.
- [ ] No record that passed before fails now.

Score: 8995 -> 8995 of 10012

Opened by the yantra runner. A person merges.

<details>
<summary>Report of agent start 1, as plain text</summary>

```text
# Report: ticket 20, comparison and boolean operators

## 1. What changed

- `src/lexer.rs`: six new tokens for `=`/`==`, `<>`/`!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`. `<<` and `>>` are explicit lexer errors, and `!` alone, `|`, `&`, `~` stay errors.
- `src/select.rs`: four new parser levels above the arithmetic (`OR`, `AND`, the `=`/`IS` row, the `<` row) and a `compare` function.
- `NOT` is read in `unary`, with an operand at the `=` row. SQLite accepts `NOT` as the operand of any operator and lets it take the rest of the expression up to `AND`/`OR`; this reproduces that.
- `IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL` accept only the literal `NULL` on the right. `1 IS NULL + 1` is an explicit error, because SQLite reads it as `1 IS (NULL + 1)`.
- Tests: 7 new tests in `select.rs` and 1 in `lexer.rs`. The old "must be an error" entries for `1 = 1`, `1 < 2`, `1 AND 1`, `NOT 1` and `1 IS NULL` are removed.
- `README.md`: the Status section lists the new operators and their rules.
- `tests/slt/baseline.txt`: not changed. The measured count is still 8995.

Sources (rule 5): the precedence table in section 2 of https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html, and `yt sqlite` (SQLite 3.46.1) for each expected value. The code comments quote the statements and answers.

## 2. Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Check that I ran | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Comparisons give 1 or 0, NULL operand gives NULL | `yt sqlite`: `SELECT 1 = 1, 1 == 2, 1 <> 2, 1 != 1, 1 < 2, 2 <= 2, 1 > 2, 2 >= 3` and the same with NULL operands. Unit test `comparison_gives_one_zero_or_null` | SQLite: `1,0,1,0,1,1,0,0` and eight NULLs. Test passes with the same values |
| `NOT`, `AND`, `OR` three-valued logic | `yt sqlite`: all 10 operand pairs of `AND` and of `OR`, and `NOT 0, NOT 1, NOT 5, NOT - 3, NOT NULL, NOT NOT 7`. Unit test `not_and_or_follow_three_valued_logic` | SQLite: `NULL AND 0` = 0, `NULL OR 1` = 1, `NOT NULL` = NULL, `2 AND - 3` = 1. Test passes with the same values |
| `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` give 1 or 0 | `yt sqlite`: `SELECT 1 IS NULL, NULL IS NULL, 1 IS NOT NULL, NULL IS NOT NULL, 1 / 0 IS NULL, 0 IS NULL`. Unit test `is_null_and_is_not_null_give_one_or_zero` | SQLite: `0,1,1,0,1,0`. Test passes |
| Precedence of the table, left to right in one row | `yt sqlite`: 50 expressions across 7 statements (for example `1 = 2 < 3`, `3 > 2 > 1`, `NOT 1 = 2`, `1 OR 0 AND 0`, `NULL IS NULL = 1`, `- NOT 0 = 5`). Unit tests `precedence_of_comparison_and_boolean_operators` and `not_as_an_operand_takes_the_rest_of_the_expression` | Tests pass with SQLite's values |
| Result is an integer, usable in arithmetic, functions, aggregates | `yt sqlite`: `SELECT (1 < 2) + (2 < 3), (1 = 1) * 5, - (1 = 1), COALESCE(NULL = 1, 7), NULLIF(1 = 1, 1), COUNT(NULL = 1), SUM(2 > 1), MAX(1 AND NULL), MIN(NOT 0), CAST(1 < 2 AS INTEGER)`. Unit test `comparison_result_is_an_integer_operand` | SQLite: `2,5,-1,7,NULL,0,1,NULL,1,1`. Test passes |
| Each other operator is an error | Unit test `other_operators_are_errors` (62 statements) and the lexer test `rejects_unsupported_text` | Tests pass: each one is an error |
| Baseline has the exact pass count, not lower | `yt check` | `slt: random/expr/slt_good_0.test 8995/10012`, same as before, baseline test passes |
| No record that passed before fails now | `yt check` | The count is equal, 8995. I did not compare the set of passing records one by one. The change only accepts input that was an error before |

`yt check` was green (fmt, clippy, 37 unit tests, 10 harness tests) before the README edit. After the README edit I ran `yt failures 3`, which compiled and gave 8995 again. I did not run the full `yt check` again after the README edit.

## 3. Known differences from SQLite

- **The score did not go up.** The two records I saw that use these operators (lines 92 and 2444) have them inside `CASE`, so they still fail until the `CASE` ticket.
- `AND` and `OR` compute both operands. `SELECT 0 AND 9223372036854775807 + 1` gives 0 in SQLite 3.46.1 and an integer overflow error here.
- Values with SQLite, errors here: `IS`/`IS NOT` with a right side that is not the literal `NULL`, including `1 IS (NULL)`, `1 IS NULL + 1` (SQLite: 0), `1 IS NOT NULL - 1` (SQLite: 1) and `1 IS NOT NOT NULL` (SQLite: 1).
- Values with SQLite, errors here, as the ticket asks: `~`, `||`, `&`, `|`, `<<`, `>>`, `BETWEEN`, `IN`, `LIKE`, `GLOB`, `ISNULL`, `NOTNULL`, postfix `NOT NULL`, `IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM`.

## 4. Text for new tickets

- `CASE` expressions, both forms. This is the ticket that turns the new operators into passing records.
- `AND`/`OR` should not fail on an error in an operand that SQLite does not need. Needs a source for SQLite's exact evaluation rule first; `yt sqlite` line 43 shows `abs(-9223372036854775807 - 1) AND 0` gives 0 there.
- `IS` and `IS NOT` with a general right side, and `IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM`.
- `ISNULL`, `NOTNULL` and postfix `NOT NULL`.
- `CAST(<expr> AS REAL)` and `AVG`: both appear in the first 40 failing records.
- `CREATE TABLE` and `INSERT`: the first 12 failing records.

## 5. Review findings

Not a review round.
```

</details>

pull_requests.title: CAST to INTEGER in SELECT without FROM
pull_requests.description:
Closes #18

Ticket: https://github.com/bettersandeep/lekha/issues/18

Acceptance criteria from the ticket:
- [ ] `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` returns the value of an integer expression without change, and NULL for NULL.
- [ ] `CAST`, `AS` and `INTEGER` are case-insensitive, and white space is allowed before the `(`.
- [ ] The argument can be each expression that the engine supports, an aggregate included, and a `CAST` can be inside each of them.
- [ ] Each other target type is an error for now. A missing `AS`, a missing type and extra tokens inside the parentheses are errors.
- [ ] `tests/slt/baseline.txt` has the new exact pass count. The number goes up.
- [ ] No record that passed before fails now.

Score: 7981 -> 8995 of 10012

Opened by the yantra runner. A person merges.

<details>
<summary>Report of agent start 1, as plain text</summary>

```text
# Report: ticket 18, CAST to INTEGER in SELECT without FROM

## 1. What changed

- `src/select.rs`: new `Parser::cast`, reached from `unary` when the word `CAST` is followed by `(`.
  - It parses `CAST ( expr AS INTEGER )` and returns the argument without change.
  - Each other type name gives `CAST to <name> is not supported`.
  - A missing `AS`, a missing type and extra tokens give the existing "unsupported syntax" error.
- `src/select.rs` tests:
  - Four new tests: `cast_to_integer_returns_the_argument`, `cast_ignores_case_and_white_space`, `cast_with_each_other_expression`, `cast_errors`.
  - Removed `SELECT CAST(NULL AS INTEGER)` and `SELECT CAST(1 AS INTEGER)` from two older "must be an error" lists, because they are supported now.
- `tests/slt/baseline.txt`: 7981 to 8995.
- `README.md`: the Status part names `CAST` and gives the new score.

Sources for the SQLite rules (rule 5): the syntax is from https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#castexpr, and the values are from `yt sqlite`, which reported SQLite 3.46.1. Both are named in the code comment.

`yt check` passed on the final state: fmt, clippy, 29 unit tests, 10 harness tests, `slt: random/expr/slt_good_0.test 8995/10012`.

## 2. Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Check that I ran | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` returns an integer value without change, and NULL for NULL | `yt sqlite` on `SELECT CAST(1 AS INTEGER), CAST(- 5 AS INTEGER), CAST(NULL AS INTEGER), CAST(2 * 3 + 1 AS INTEGER), CAST(1 / 0 AS INTEGER)` gave `1, -5, NULL, 7, NULL`. generated_descriptions.long:
```
## Summary

This PR adds support for `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` in `SELECT` statements without `FROM`, which was previously rejected as invalid syntax. It closes issue #18 and raises the SLT baseline pass count from **7981** to **8995**.

The change is intentionally narrow: only `INTEGER` casts are supported for now. All other target types remain errors, as do malformed `CAST` expressions such as missing `AS`, missing type names, or extra tokens inside the parentheses.

---

## Why this was needed

Before this PR, the expression engine supported integer literals, `NULL`, arithmetic, parentheses, and a small set of functions/aggregates, but not SQL-style casts. The ticket required support for:

- `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` behaving as a no-op over integer values
- `NULL` remaining `NULL`
- case-insensitive `CAST`, `AS`, and `INTEGER`
- whitespace before `(`
- casts working on any expression the engine already supports, including aggregates
- unsupported target types and malformed syntax producing errors

This addressed a gap in expression coverage and brought the engine closer to SQLite-like behavior for this specific construct.

---

## What changed

### `src/select.rs`

The core parser was extended to recognize `CAST` as a special expression form instead of treating it like a normal function call.

#### New `Parser::cast`
A new parsing function was added that handles:

- `CAST(`
- followed by an expression
- then `AS`
- then `INTEGER`
- then `)`

Behavior implemented:

- returns the parsed value unchanged
- accepts case-insensitive keywords
- supports whitespace before the `(`
- rejects any type other than `INTEGER`
- rejects malformed forms with the existing syntax error path

#### `unary()` dispatch updated
The unary-expression parser now checks whether a word followed by `(` is `CAST`. If so, it routes to the new `cast()` parser; otherwise it continues handling regular function calls.

This makes `CAST` a first-class expression form in the grammar.

#### Tests added/updated
Several new unit tests were added to cover the accepted and rejected cases:

- `cast_to_integer_returns_the_argument`
- `cast_ignores_case_and_white_space`
- `cast_with_each_other_expression`
- `cast_errors`

These tests verify:

- identity behavior for integer values
- `NULL` propagation
- case insensitivity
- whitespace tolerance
- nested casts
- casts around aggregates and casts inside other expressions
- error handling for unsupported types and malformed syntax

Some older tests were also updated to remove `CAST(NULL AS INTEGER)` / `CAST(1 AS INTEGER)` from lists of expected failures, since those expressions are now supported.

---

### `tests/slt/baseline.txt`

The SLT baseline score was updated to reflect the new accepted records:

- from `7981`
- to `8995`

This confirms the new syntax is now recognized in the baseline test corpus.

---

### `README.md`

The documentation was updated to reflect the new expression support and the higher pass score.

Changes include:

- adding `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` to the list of supported expression forms
- documenting that `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` returns its argument unchanged
- stating that `CAST`, `AS`, and `INTEGER` are case-insensitive
- noting that other target types and missing type specifications are errors
- updating the recorded pass score from `7981` to `8995`

---

## Affected areas of the codebase

### Parser / expression handling
- `src/select.rs`
  - expression parsing
  - keyword dispatch in unary expressions
  - cast syntax validation
  - error reporting for invalid casts

### Test coverage
- `src/select.rs` unit tests
  - new coverage for valid casts, invalid casts, nested expressions, aggregates, and syntax errors

### Documentation / project status
- `README.md`
  - supported expression grammar
  - documented cast semantics
  - current test score

### SLT baseline
- `tests/slt/baseline.txt`
  - updated pass count for the expression suite

---

## Result

After this change, the engine now supports `CAST(<expr> AS INTEGER)` in `SELECT` expressions without `FROM`, while preserving existing behavior for all previously passing records and keeping unsupported cast forms as errors.

pull_requests.title: Add COUNT, MIN, MAX and SUM
pull_requests.description:
Closes #11

Ticket: https://github.com/bettersandeep/lekha/issues/11

Score on `random/expr/slt_good_0.test`: **5021 -> 7981 of 10012**.

Acceptance criteria from the ticket:
- [x] `COUNT(*)` returns 1. `COUNT([ALL | DISTINCT] expr)` returns 1 when `expr` is not NULL, and 0 when it is NULL.
- [x] `MIN`, `MAX` and `SUM`, each with one argument and an optional `ALL` or `DISTINCT`, return the value of the argument. A NULL argument gives NULL.
- [x] An aggregate can be a part of a larger expression, and one select list can hold aggregates and plain expressions.
- [x] An aggregate inside the argument of an aggregate is an error, as in SQLite.
- [x] `MIN` and `MAX` with two or more arguments are errors for now. `AVG`, `TOTAL` and `GROUP_CONCAT` are errors for now.
- [x] `tests/slt/baseline.txt` has the new exact pass count. The number goes up.
- [x] No record that passed before fails now.

How it was checked:
- Each criterion was run as a query against the built engine and against SQLite 3.49.1.
- The set of passing records before this change is a subset of the set after it: 5021 before, 7981 after, 0 lost.
- 38000 random queries were compared with SQLite 3.49.1. 34726 give the same row, 1735 are an error in both, and 1539 are an error here where SQLite gives a value. No query gives a different value.
- All 2031 records that still fail are errors for features that are not there: CAST, CASE, AVG, comparison operators, and the 12 table statements.

Known differences from SQLite, all an error here where SQLite gives a value: `COUNT()`, `MIN` and `MAX` with two or more arguments, an aggregate inside those, `FILTER`, `OVER` and `ORDER BY` on an aggregate, and integer overflow. None is in the ticket. They are written up as text for later tickets.

Source for the behaviour: https://www.sqlite.org/lang_aggfunc.html and https://www.sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html.

pull_requests.title: Add NULL, COALESCE and NULLIF
pull_requests.description:
Closes #10

Ticket: https://github.com/bettersandeep/lekha/issues/10

Score on `random/expr/slt_good_0.test`: **4577 -> 5021 of 10012**.

Acceptance criteria from the ticket:
- [x] `NULL` is an expression. Unary and binary arithmetic with a NULL operand gives NULL.
- [x] `COALESCE(a, b, ...)` takes two or more arguments and returns the first one that is not NULL, or NULL when all are NULL.
- [x] `NULLIF(a, b)` takes exactly two arguments. It returns NULL when `a` equals `b`, and `a` in each other case. A NULL argument never equals a value.
- [x] Function names are case-insensitive, and white space is allowed before the `(`.
- [x] A wrong number of arguments is an error. An error inside an argument is an error for the whole statement, also for an argument that SQLite does not evaluate.
- [x] Each other function name is still an error.
- [x] `tests/slt/baseline.txt` has the new exact pass count. The number goes up.
- [x] No record that passed before fails now.

How it was checked:
- Each criterion was run as a query against the built engine and against SQLite 3.49.1.
- The set of passing records before this change is a subset of the set after it: 4577 before, 5021 after, 0 lost.
- 26000 random queries were compared with SQLite 3.49.1. 23190 give the same row, 939 are an error in both, and 1871 are an error here where SQLite gives a value (integer overflow, the literal 9223372036854775808, and an error in an argument that SQLite does not evaluate). No query gives a different value.

Sources for the behaviour: https://www.sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html (coalesce, nullif) and https://www.sqlite.org/nulls.html.

The first commit also made a statement of more than 1000 tokens an error. That is not in the ticket, so the second commit removes it. It goes into its own ticket.

Also updated tests/baseline.txt with the new exact pass count and removed an unrelated statement-size limit change from the earlier commit.

pull_requests.title: Evaluate integer arithmetic in SELECT without FROM
pull_requests.description:
Closes #2

Ticket: https://github.com/bettersandeep/yantra-sql/issues/2

First capability of the engine: `SELECT` with integer arithmetic and no FROM clause.
Score on SQLite's test file `random/expr/slt_good_0.test`: **0 -> 4577 of 10012**.

Acceptance criteria from the ticket:
- [x] `SELECT [ALL | DISTINCT] <item> {, <item>}` with no FROM clause returns one row. An item is `<expr> [[AS] <alias>]`.
- [x] `<expr>` supports integer literals, unary `+` and `-`, binary `+ - * / %` with normal precedence, and parentheses.
- [x] SQLite semantics: integer division truncates toward zero, `%` takes the sign of the left operand, and division or modulo by zero gives NULL.
- [x] Each other input returns an error and never a guessed value.
- [x] `tests/slt/baseline.txt` has the new exact pass count.
- [x] The test files and the harness are not changed.

How it was checked:
- All 5435 records that still fail are errors for features that are not there yet. None is a wrong value.
- 30000 random arithmetic queries were compared with SQLite 3.49.1. 29890 match. The other 110 hit integer overflow, where this engine returns an error as the ticket says and SQLite changes to a real number.

Known differences from SQLite:
- Integer overflow in `+ - *` is an error here. SQLite returns a real.
- A keyword is never accepted as an alias. SQLite accepts some.
- A trailing `;`, a `--` comment, hex literals and `1_000` are errors here.
- SQLite rejects an expression with 1000 or more chained operators. This engine evaluates it.
